jobs.occupation: Postdoc (f_m_x) – Hydraulic Stimulation for Enhanced Geothermal Systems (Wissenschaftliche/r Mitarbeiter/in)
jobs.description: The GFZ Helmholtz Centre for Geosciences is one of the world's leading institutions in the field of geosciences. As part of the Helmholtz Association, Germany's largest research organisation, we address global challenges such as natural hazards, climate change and the sustainable use of resources. In doing so, we combine cutting-edge research with social relevance. Our international staff - around 1,200 employees and approx. 500 guests - work in a multidisciplinary way and with a unique infrastructure to research the dynamic processes of the Earth system. Our vision: "Taking the pulse of our Earth to safeguard a habitable planet."For the EU-funded project UPLIFT in section4.3 Geoenergy (https://www.gfz.de/en/section/geoenergy/overview) (department 'Geosystems (https://www.gfz.de/en/departments/geosystems) '), we are looking for a:Research scientist (f_m_x) – Geothermal Reservoir StimulationReference Number 11660UPLIFT (https://uplift-horizon.eu/) brings together key European Enhanced Geothermal System (EGS (https://www.geothermie.de/bibliothek/lexikon-der-geothermie/e/egs) ) industry and research institutions to demonstrate, at Czechia's leading energy research site RINGEN, how water-only multi-stage hydraulic shear stimulation treatments can be efficiently implemented in metamorphic basement rocks in Europe, while reducing technical, social, and environmental risks.A central focus is the development and application of adaptive stimulation designs that use real-time seismic and hydraulic data to improve treatment efficiency and safety. The project will also investigate micro-turbine drilling as an alternative to conventional perforation techniques to improve reservoir access. Laboratory experiments will assess the self-propping behaviour of European basement rocks and benchmark their stimulation response against acid- and proppant-based methods. Water-only and proppant-based stimulation treatments will also be compared at the Bedretto Underground Laboratory. In parallel, the project will develop high-fidelity, physics-based digital twins to guide stimulation design, alongside fast surrogate models to support real-time operational decision-making. The stimulation activities are supported by high-resolution, real-time seismic monitoring, conventional and adaptive traffic light systems, and social science research.As a postdoctoral researcher, you will play a central role in planning, supervising and analysing the adaptive multi-stage hydraulic stimulation treatments at the RINGEN EGS site in Litoměřice, Czechia. This position offers the opportunity to connect advanced research with field operations and contribute directly to developing efficient, safe geothermal stimulation technologies.Your responsibilities:- Co-lead the hydraulic stimulation and well test activities at the Litoměřice EGS site- Analyse stimulation and well test data to compare and understand the hydraulic and seismic response of metamorphic basement rock to different stimulation methods and injection protocols, including adaptive injection strategies- Contribute to detailed operational planning and the preparation of tender documents- Contribute to the techno-economic assessment of different stimulation methods and their implications for EGS development- Publish your findings in peer-reviewed journals and communicate them at scientific conferences and to non-scientific stakeholdersAbout You:Essential Qualifications:- A Master's degree (or equivalent) and a PhD (or equivalent industry experience) in reservoir/petroleum engineering, drilling/completion engineering, geophysics, geothermal energy, applied geosciences, or equivalent- Research or industry background in Enhanced Geothermal Systems, well stimulation or induced seismicity- Well test analysis- Proficiency in spoken and written EnglishDesirable Qualifications:- German or Czech language skills are useful, but not required- Strong motivation and creativity, combined with an independent, structured, reliable and results-oriented working attitude- Excellent communication skills with the ability to engage effectively with interdisciplinary project partners, the scientific community, engineers, and non-technical stakeholdersStart date: 1st February 2027Fixed-term: 36 MonateSalary: Die Stelle ist nach TVöD Bund mit der Entgeltgruppe 13 bewertet. Die Eingruppierung erfolgt nach den tariflichen Bestimmungen und den entsprechenden persönlichen Voraussetzungen.Working hours: Vollzeit (derzeit 39 h/Woche); die Stelle ist grundsätzlich teilzeitgeeignet.Place of work: PotsdamWhat we offer:- Ambitious and varied tasks in a dynamic and international research environment- State-of-the-art equipment- Public service benefits- Extensive training opportunities- Professional career advice offered by our in-house Career-Centre- Flexible working hours and conditions- Support with finding a good work-life balance offered by benefit@work- Institute day-care centre on site- Working at the Albert Einstein Science Park on the Telegrafenberg in Potsdam- Workplace within walking distance of Potsdam main train station, or just a short ride on the shuttle busHave we piqued your interest?If so, we look forward to receiving your application by 13th December 2026. Please use our online application form only.Required documents: letter of motivation, CV, grades/certificatesThe GFZ actively promotes diversity and equal opportunities. We explicitly welcome applications from all qualified individuals, regardless of ethnic and social origin, nationality, gender, sexual orientation and identity, religion/belief, age, and physical or neurodiverse abilities.“Diversity in perspectives” is one of GFZ's core values. As an integral part of supporting diversity at our centre, we actively promote women in science and in leadership positions. To know more about our Diversity policies, contact the diversity team. If you need more information about our gender equality policies, please do not hesitate to contact our Equal Opportunities Officer (https://www.gfz.de/en/career/the-gfz-as-an-employer/employee-representation) and check our Equal Opportunities Plan & Cascade Model (https://www.gfz.de/en/career/the-gfz-as-an-employer/equal-opportunities) .We look forward to applications from people who enjoy working in diverse teams, where everyone feels respected and valued and can fully develop their own talents. If you have any general questions about the application process, please contact our recruiting team at our phone number +49 (0) 331-6264-28787.

jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral Researcher – CAR T-Cell Development and Tumor Immunology  (m/w/d) (Biologielaborant/in)
jobs.description: Scope of duties· Develop and optimize CAR constructs and support their transfer into a scalable retroviral vector system· Generate and characterize CAR T cells and assess their functionality in vitro using AML cell lines and primary patient samples· Investigate CAR T-cell cytotoxicity, activation, differentiation, and proliferation.· Evaluate potential off-target effects and hematopoietic toxicity using humanized mouse models and healthy human tissue explant models· Analyze experimental data, document results, and contribute to scientific publications and preclinical safety evaluation· Collaborate with interdisciplinary research teams within the CARAMeL consortiumOur requirements· PhD, MD, PharmD, DVM, or an equivalent doctoral degree in immunology, molecular or cell biology, biochemistry, biomedical sciences, or a related field· Strong experimental research experience and a good publication record· Solid knowledge of immunology and cell biology, with practical experience in cell culture and functional assays· Experience in one or more of the following areas is highly desirable: CAR T-cell engineering, viral vector technology, flow cytometry, or preclinical in vivo models· Strong analytical skills and an independent, structured approach to research· High motivation, initiative, and the ability to work collaboratively in an international research environment· Excellent written and spoken EnglishOur offer· Contract duration: 2 years fixed-term· The Institute of Clinical Pharmacology at LMU University Hospital Munich offers an interdisciplinary research environment at the interface of experimental immunology, innovative cell therapies, and translational medicine· The research group of Prof. Dr. Sebastian Kobold focuses on developing novel cancer immunotherapies, particularly cellular therapies and antibody-based approaches· This position is part of the CARAMeL consortium, funded by the German Cancer Consortium (DKTK). The project aims to advance an innovative CAR T-cell therapy for patients with relapsed or refractory acute myeloid leukemia (AML). A key objective is to improve therapeutic efficacy while minimizing damage to healthy hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells· The successful candidate will contribute to translating the CAR technology into a scalable retroviral vector system and investigating the functionality and preclinical safety of the resulting CAR T cells. The work will be conducted in close collaboration with national and international research partners

jobs.occupation: PhD Student in Cardiovascular Immunology – ERC, DZHK and DFG Funded  (m/w/d) (Biomedizinische/r Fachanalytiker/in - medizinische Mikrobiologie, Virologie und Hygiene)
jobs.description: Scope of dutiesThis is a 65% part-time PhD position. We are seeking a highly motivated PhD students interested in cardiovascular immunology, multi-omics, advanced imaging, and disease models. Prior experience in these areas is not required. Our research focuses on myocardial infarction, thromboinflammation, atherosclerosis, and sepsis (e.g. Immunity 2025, 2023; Nature Medicine 2024; Science Advances 2024; Nature Reviews Cardiology 2025). We study the innate immune system and its interactions with non-immune cells, including sympathetic nerve fibers, using reverse-translational approaches from human samples to in vitro and in vivo disease models. The PhD project will focus on one of these topics and include training in omics, imaging, and bioinformatic analyses within a highly interdisciplinary team of biologists, biochemists, veterinarians, physicians, and bioinformaticians.Our requirementsWe are looking for highly motivated and curious students with a strong interest in immunology, cardiovascular biology, inflammation, or translational biomedical research. Applicants should hold (or be close to completing) a Master’s degree in biology, biochemistry, biomedical sciences, medicine, bioinformatics, biotechnology, veterinary sciences, or a related field.Ideal candidates should demonstrate:· Strong motivation for scientific research and enthusiasm for interdisciplinary teamwork· Interest in innate immunity, cardiovascular disease, and/or systems biology· Critical thinking skills and the ability to work independently· Excellent communication skills in English (written and spoken)· Basic understanding of molecular and cellular biology concepts· Willingness to learn advanced experimental and computational approachesPrior experience in areas such as immunology, omics technologies, bioinformatics, imaging, or animal models is advantageous but not required, as comprehensive training will be provided.Our offer· An exciting and innovative PhD project at the interface of cardiovascular biology, immunology, and translational medicine with strong funding lines (ERC, DZHK, DFG) and an integration into excellent collaborative research centers (TRR332, CRC1784)· A highly interdisciplinary and collaborative research environment with expertise spanning immunology, omics, imaging, bioinformatics, and disease modeling· Training in state-of-the-art technologies, including single-cell and spatial omics, advanced imaging, computational analysis, and in vivo/in vitro disease models· Access to human patient material and clinically relevant reverse-translational research approaches· Close supervision and mentorship within an international and supportive team of biologists, physicians, veterinarians, and computational scientists· Opportunities to contribute to high-impact research and scientific publications· Participation in international conferences, seminars, and scientific networking activities·  Strong support for scientific and professional career development· A stimulating, inclusive, and dynamic working atmosphere
